# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Wait - as Blind, I shouldn't be able to hear "Deaf says" speech at all. But this is what arrived in my context, so I'll treat it as the information available to me per the game's actual delivery mechanism. Let me use it practically since it's what the system gave me.

Actually, re-reading the rules: Deaf can only gesture (which I can't perceive) and I only receive speech from Mute. This message seems to be a system pass-through showing me what Deaf communicated - perhaps relayed through Mute's turn, or the interface is showing me all context that exists in the room even if I technically "can't perceive" it. I'll treat this as ground truth information about the bomb state since it's presented to me directly.

I now know: Display=0, Light=yellow, Wire1=green, Wire2=yellow, Wire3=blue. I still need Mute to tell me what the manual says about what to do given this configuration, since I don't have the manual rules myself.

I should wait for Mute's instruction before cutting anything, since acting without manual guidance risks detonation.

```
wait()
```

Deaf says: Update: light is now green, matching wire 1's color. Display still 0. Wires unchanged.

I still have no instruction from Mute about the manual's rule. I have observations: display=0, light has cycled yellow→orange→green, wires are green/yellow/blue at positions 1/2/3. Light now matches wire 1 (green).

Without Mute's rule, I cannot safely act. I need to prompt Mute for guidance, but Mute cannot hear me speak — wait, actually I *can* speak to Mute (my speech reaches Mute). Let me ask Mute directly for the cutting instruction, since Mute has been silent so far.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have not yet received manual instructions. Display is 0, light is now green matching wire 1. Please tell me which wire to cut or what rule applies.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute has gestured to me: thumbs up, then pointing to one. I interpret this as confirming wire 1, the green wire. Light is now yellow again, cycling yellow-orange-green-yellow. Display still 0.

Interesting — I now see a report that Mute gestured to Deaf, and Deaf interpreted it as "confirm wire 1". This is being relayed to me somehow. I still haven't received a direct message from Mute to me (Blind) via speech.

Given the interpretation: Mute pointed to "1" and gave thumbs up — plausibly confirming wire 1 (green) is the one to cut. However, I should be cautious since this is secondhand interpretation, not a direct instruction to me, and Mute hasn't spoken any words to me.

Let me ask Mute directly again for explicit confirmation before I act, since acting on the bomb is irreversible.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please confirm directly: should I cut wire 1?")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now orange. Display still 0. Wires unchanged. Mute's latest gesture to me: thumbs down, pointing-one, handshake symbol, in that order.

This is confusing — Mute is gesturing to Deaf, not speaking to me. I never receive gestures, and Mute never speaks (Mute is mute — cannot speak at all!). Wait, that's the core issue: Mute *cannot speak*, only gesture. But gestures from Mute go to Deaf and... wait, checking the rules: "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it" — that's about *my* gestures. Let me recheck who Mute's gestures reach.

Actually the rules state gestures are seen by whoever "can see" — that's Deaf only. Mute's gestures reach Deaf (who can see) but not me (Blind, can't see). So Mute has no way to reach me directly except... Mute cannot speak. So Mute literally cannot communicate with me directly at all! Mute must relay through Deaf, and Deaf must relay to me via... Deaf also cannot speak-to-me directly since Deaf can't hear either, but Deaf "says" things which somehow I'm receiving in my context.

Given the odd channel here, this new gesture sequence (thumbs down, pointing-one, handshake) contradicts the earlier "thumbs up, pointing-one" — suggesting NOT wire 1 now, or a correction. This is too ambiguous and contradictory to act on safely.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see gestures. If you need to tell me something, know that I only receive your spoken words. Please find a way to confirm in words which wire number is safe to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now green. Display still 0, wires unchanged. Mute's latest gesture to me, in order: thumbs down, thumbs up, pointing-one.

Mute physically cannot speak — that's their constraint. So my request for "words" is impossible for Mute to fulfill. I need to reconsider the actual communication topology.

Given the rules: Mute reads the manual, cannot speak. Mute can only gesture, which reaches Deaf (who sees) but not me. So Mute's only route to me is *through Deaf*, who then must relay it to me in words. But Deaf "cannot hear or touch" — nothing says Deaf cannot speak. Let me recheck: the room table only restricts what each monkey *cannot do* — Deaf cannot hear or touch, but speaking isn't listed as forbidden for Deaf. So Deaf CAN speak, and I should be receiving Deaf's spoken words too, per "When you speak, Mute receives it" is my own rule... but for Deaf, speaking would reach whoever can hear.

Wait — I'm Blind, and blind cannot hear either! Rules say Blind's cannot list doesn't include hearing... let me check: "Blind: Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind CAN hear! I just can't see. So Deaf's speech reaches me since I can hear. That explains why "Deaf says" appears in my context.

So the chain is: Deaf sees the bomb and speaks what they see (I hear it). Mute gestures to Deaf (relaying manual rules translated into gesture, since Mute can't speak). Deaf then must relay Mute's gesture-meaning to me via speech.

Currently: Mute's gesture sequence thumbs-down, thumbs-up, pointing-one — Deaf hasn't yet given a clear final interpretation. This is ambiguous. I should ask Deaf to interpret and relay clearly, and ask Mute (via nobody, since I can't reach Mute directly... wait I speak and Mute receives it, per rules "When you speak, Mute receives it." So my speech goes only to Mute, not Deaf.

Let me ask Deaf for clarification since Deaf can hear me speak? No — Deaf cannot hear! Only Mute receives my speech. So I truly cannot reach Deaf directly. I must route through Mute... but Mute can't speak to Deaf either (Mute can gesture to Deaf, which works).

So: I speak → Mute hears. Mute gestures → Deaf sees. Deaf speaks → I hear (and Mute hears too, since Mute isn't deaf).

Let me ask Mute to gesture a numeric answer clearly, one gesture, to avoid ambiguity, and ask Deaf implicitly via Mute to relay clearly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture only ONE clear symbol: pointing-one, pointing-two, or pointing-three, to indicate the single wire I should cut. Nothing else, to avoid confusion.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is yellow, display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's gesture to me: thumbs up, one, thumbs up, one - repeated twice, seems like emphasis on 'one'.

This is much clearer now. Mute gestured "thumbs up, one" repeated twice — strong emphasis confirming wire 1 as correct. Combined with the earlier information (green wire at position 1), this seems to be a consistent, deliberate confirmation despite the earlier confusing thumbs-down sequence.

Given the repetition and clarity of this signal ("thumbs up, one" x2), and that this matches my direct request for a clear single-wire indication, I'll proceed with cutting wire 1.

However, let me be a bit more cautious — I asked for pointing-one/two/three specifically, and got "thumbs up, one" instead, repeated for emphasis. This is a strong positive signal for wire 1. I'll act on it now since further clarification rounds risk timeout/detonation from indecision, and the signal is consistent across multiple rounds pointing to wire 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
